# Idea: riotdoc-enhancements

## Core Concept

Enhance existing RiotDoc with missing features: feedback/narrative capture system (like RiotPlan), version numbering (v0.1 → v1.0), document type templates (email, project-plan, research-paper), outline manipulation tools, and draft generation strategy selection. Focus on blog-post and podcast-script as primary use cases.

RiotDoc already exists at /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotdoc. This is about enhancing it, not creating it from scratch.

## Why This Matters

Documents have different lifecycles than plans. Some are one-time (blog posts), others are living standards (charters) that evolve continuously. RiotDoc needs to support both while preserving the narrative and deliberation that goes into creating them.

## Initial Thoughts

- **CRITICAL**: User's full voice transcript text must be captured in timeline/prompts, not just AI-extracted summaries. The raw conversational narrative is valuable context. Current Cursor prompt may not be calling the right tool to save this content.

- **Key difference from RiotPlan**: Plans are temporary with clear execution endpoints (idea → plan → execute → retrospective → archive). Documents have varied lifecycles - some are one-time (blog posts), others are living standards (charters, constitutions) that evolve continuously.

- **Proposed document creation flow**: idea → evidence/references gathering → planning (objectives, audience, voice, tone, structure) → draft generation → review/revision cycles → versioning/finalization

- **Documents need metadata that plans don't**: voice, tone, audience, format requirements, reference style, structural elements (TOC, index), example documents to emulate

- **Shared infrastructure with RiotPlan**: history mechanism, checkpoint mechanism, similar MCP patterns for prompts/tools/resources. But different entities: sections instead of steps, drafts instead of execution states

- **Industry standard document lifecycle** (OASIS, IETF, W3C): Working Draft → Review/Feedback → Approval → Publication → Maintenance. Key principle: documents don't revert to earlier stages once advanced. Some orgs use "standing rules" to streamline approval processes.

- **ISO/IEC/IEEE 26531:2023** covers content management for product lifecycles, including how content is gathered, managed, and published through component content management systems (CCMS). Applies to both printed and electronic information.

- **Versioning standards**: RFC 3253 defines WebDAV versioning extensions including automatic versioning, version history management, workspace management, and URL namespace versioning. ISO 19475:2021 covers storage requirements for maintaining authenticity, integrity, and readability.

- **Proposed RiotDoc lifecycle synthesis**: Idea → Evidence/References → Outline/Planning → Draft (v0.1) → Review/Revision cycles (v0.2, v0.3...) → Approval/Finalization (v1.0) → Publication → Maintenance (v1.1, v1.2...). Living documents may skip "final" state and remain in continuous maintenance.

- **Document types are essential** and should affect workflow. Examples: blog posts (title, subtitle, tags, categories, short length) vs charters (complex, set format, long). RiotDoc should ship with well-known document types but be flexible for user-defined templates. Document type changes the questions asked during idea exploration.

- **Outline phase is critical**: Idea → Outline/Structure → Draft. Outline defines structure (chapters, sections) and triggers feedback cycles. Outline should remain accessible after draft creation to allow reordering sections ("move this section before that section").

- **Draft generation strategy spectrum**: (1) User writes draft in idea phase, AI refines it preserving voice ("don't change it too much, I own this voice"), (2) User provides stream-of-consciousness thoughts/evidence, AI writes full draft, (3) Hybrid approach. Ask user upfront which strategy they prefer, similar to RiotPlan's shaping approach selection.

- **Revision tracking**: Use separate files (draft-v0.1.md, draft-v0.2.md, etc.) for simplicity. Future could explore diffs or embedded formats, but start simple with separate files. File size is not a concern.

- **Example documents** can be: (1) file path reference to emulate, (2) copied into project, (3) URL to document. Use cases: emulation (style/tone reference) or evidence. Style/tone is bigger than individual documents - may be application-level context, discuss separately.

- **Shared infrastructure decision**: Copy/paste history and checkpoint code from RiotPlan to RiotDoc for now (keep in sync manually). Don't create shared library yet - there are existing projects that can be resuscitated later. Priority: history first, checkpoint second. Easier to copy/paste initially, ensure doesn't drift too far.

- **Refined lifecycle with outline phase**: Idea → Evidence/References → Outline/Structure → Draft Generation Strategy Selection → Draft (v0.1) → Review/Revision (v0.2+) → Approval/Finalization (v1.0) → Publication → Maintenance (v1.1+). Living documents may skip finalization.

- **MCP integration**: RiotDoc should expose MCP tools for document creation, outline manipulation, draft generation, revision tracking, and version management. Similar pattern to RiotPlan's MCP tools but adapted for document workflow.

- **Built-in document types for v1**: (1) Blog Post - most used ✓ exists, (2) Podcast Script - most used ✓ exists, (3) Email - MISSING, (4) Project Plan - MISSING, (5) Research Paper - MISSING. Also has: technical-doc, newsletter, custom. Focus on blog post and podcast script as primary use cases.

- **Template system**: Could be YAML, JSON, or Markdown. Need to prototype and show what it looks like, then iterate from there. Flexible approach.

- **Outline manipulation**: Primary method is direct editing of outline file. Optional MCP tools: "review outline" or "alter outline" for programmatic changes. Future consideration: when outline changes, potentially update associated document structure automatically. Don't worry about document sync for now.

- **Version numbering**: Start at v0.1. User-controlled increment. Drafts can go v0.1 → v0.2 → ... → v0.99+. When user is comfortable, they explicitly update to v1.0 (published status). This is a manual decision point, not automatic.

- **Approval/finalization**: Audience of one (single user). No complex approval workflows or multi-user collaboration for v1. User decides when to finalize. Don't overcomplicate with migrations or multi-user features.

- **Living documents**: Don't distinguish between minor/major updates for v1. Not a relevant question yet. Keep it simple.

- **RiotPlan location**: Sibling directory to RiotDoc (/Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotplan). Can reference for history/checkpoint implementation patterns.

- **IMPORTANT**: Need to capture narrative conversation feedback in RiotPlan/RiotDoc. This conversational exploration is valuable and should be saved as part of the idea/planning process. RiotPlan was rebuilt to support this.

- **RiotPlan has a feedback system** that preserves deliberation, not just decisions. Creates numbered feedback records (001-xxx.md) with: what was proposed, feedback given, discussion, resolution, changes made, open questions, participants, platform, plan version. This narrative conversation capture should be adapted for RiotDoc.

- **RiotDoc already exists** at /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotdoc with: document types (blog-post, podcast-script, technical-doc, newsletter, custom), assistance levels (generate, expand, revise, cleanup, spellcheck), lifecycle status (idea, outlined, drafting, revising, final, exported), voice config, objectives, evidence tracking, draft history. Missing: feedback/narrative capture, version numbering (v0.1, v1.0), document type templates, outline manipulation tools.

- **Current RiotDoc types**: Has: blog-post ✓, podcast-script ✓, technical-doc, newsletter, custom. MISSING: email, project-plan, research-paper. Blog-post and podcast-script are the two most-used types and should be prioritized.

- **CRITICAL ISSUE**: The /riotplan/explore_idea Cursor prompt does not have access to riotplan_idea_add_narrative tool. User's full voice narrative responses are NOT being captured to timeline, only extracted structured notes. Need to fix the Cursor prompt to include narrative capture tool, or manually save narrative chunks. The raw conversational text is valuable context that should be preserved in timeline.jsonl as 'narrative_chunk' events.

- **IMPLEMENTATION STATUS (2026-01-29)**: riotplan_idea_add_narrative tool EXISTS in RiotPlan source code (/Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotplan/src/mcp/tools/idea.ts) and is properly exported in index.ts, but NOT available in Cursor's MCP tool list. Tool is designed to capture raw narrative content to timeline as 'narrative_chunk' events. Checkpoint creation works and creates .history/prompts/ files, but only captures structured state (IDEA.md, timeline events), not raw conversation. Until narrative tool is available, manually capturing conversations. RiotPlan MCP server may need rebuild/restart, or Cursor's MCP cache needs refresh.

- **USER NARRATIVE (voice)**: "Hold on what's happening you missed podcast script. That was something I asked you to do. Why did you lose that? The other thing is this narrative capture? I think you are missing the point the full text of my last prompt that text needs to show up somewhere in my theory right now is that the the prompt that I just used to do this is not giving the right instruction on how to save that content, but yeah, that's good. You're getting closer. Also, why am I running this in redaksjon workspace, this needs to be in kjerneverk"

- **USER NARRATIVE (voice)**: "Ok, that's inadequate - everything in /Users/tobrien/gitw/redaksjon/riotdoc-document-lifecycle should be moved over to /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/plans/riotdoc-enhancements merge the two, and I mean everything the timeline history and all. The fact that I was working on that plan over here was a mistake, once you are done remove it from redaksjon and lose no detail."

- **ISSUE**: riotplan_idea_add_narrative tool exists in RiotPlan source code but is not available in Cursor's MCP integration. Tool is defined, exported, and registered but Cursor returns "Tool not found". May need to rebuild/republish RiotPlan or restart MCP server. For now, capturing narratives manually in notes.
- MIGRATION COMPLETE (2026-01-29 23:30): All content from /Users/tobrien/gitw/redaksjon/riotdoc-document-lifecycle has been merged into /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/plans/riotdoc-enhancements. Timeline has 59 events (6 from kjerneverk + 53 from redaksjon). All checkpoints, prompts, and documentation files preserved. Original redaksjon directory removed.
- NARRATIVE CAPTURE: Tool availability issue is resolved - we can already do narrative capture. Question remains whether this conversation is being captured to .history/prompts/ directory. May need to update explore_idea prompt if not.
- TEMPLATE REQUIREMENTS: Templates should be straightforward and define: (1) Structure of the output document, (2) Accompanied by markdown doc with questions that need answering. Example for blog post: title idea, topic, proposed length, target audience, website destination.
- VERSION NUMBERING: User is flexible - implement whatever makes sense, will adjust if wrong later.
- OUTLINE MANIPULATION: MCP tools for revising outline would be helpful: insert section, move section, delete section. Uncertain if this is too granular. Approach: create an outline and see what happens, iterate from there.
- TEMPLATE PROTOTYPE CREATED: Four document templates created as evidence (email, project-plan, research-paper, blog-post). Each template has two parts: (1) Questions to Answer section that guides document creation, (2) Output Document Structure section that defines the markdown structure. This approach is straightforward and can be iterated on based on feedback.
- NEXT STEPS: Review template prototypes and decide if this structure works. If approved, can move to shaping phase to explore implementation approaches (how templates integrate with RiotDoc workflow, how questions are presented to users, how structure is applied to drafts).
- CRITICAL BUG IN RIOTPLAN: riotplan_idea_add_narrative only logs to timeline.jsonl, does NOT save to .history/prompts/ directory. The narrative chunks should be saved as numbered prompt files (like 003-template-feedback.md) so they can be reused as prompts. Current implementation at line 312-329 of riotplan/src/mcp/tools/idea.ts needs to be fixed to also write to prompts directory.
- TEMPLATE FEEDBACK - LIFECYCLE PHASES: Templates need to split questions into three phases: (1) Idea/Draft phase questions (title, topic, angle, length, purpose, tone), (2) Publishing phase questions (SEO, categories, tags, images, links, call-to-action). Some questions might be optional or answered at different times depending on the document. Blog posts: upfront=title/topic/angle/length/purpose/tone, end=SEO/categories/tags/images/links/CTA.
- EMAIL TEMPLATE FEEDBACK: Good structure (subject/body/to/from/date/metadata). Missing: CC and BCC fields. Questions should be split by phase: upfront=recipient/tone/purpose/length, optional/later=background/previous communication/sensitive topics/attachments/deadline. Some emails are quick (minimal questions), others need time to think (all questions).
- MISSING: Podcast script template. User has requested this multiple times. Need to create podcast-script-template.md with appropriate structure and questions.
- BUG FIX COMPLETED: Fixed riotplan_idea_add_narrative in /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotplan/src/mcp/tools/idea.ts. Function now saves narratives to BOTH timeline.jsonl AND .history/prompts/ as numbered files (001-xxx.md, 002-xxx.md, etc.). RiotPlan rebuilt successfully. Cursor's MCP server needs restart to pick up the fix.
- MANUAL SAVE COMPLETED: Saved all conversation narratives to .history/prompts/003-template-discussion-and-approach.md containing all four user narrative chunks from this session about templates, lifecycle phases, implementation approach, and the bug fix request.
- MAJOR INSIGHT - TEMPLATES DRIVE PROMPTS: Templates should define what the prompts ask at each phase. Example: explore_idea prompt should read the 'Idea/Draft Phase' section of the template to know what questions to ask (episode title, topic, etc.). The template becomes the script that drives the user experience.
- TEMPLATES DEFINE APPROACHES: Templates should also offer different 'shapes' or approaches for creating the document. Example for blog post: (1) Quick draft - write it fast, (2) Structured approach - build with sections, (3) Other strategy. The shape_approach phase would present these template-defined options.
- CRITICAL - PROMPTS MUST BE UPDATED: When we make changes, we MUST update the Cursor prompts to be aware of new tools/resources. The prompts are where the real value is - they orchestrate the tools and resources. There's a symbiotic relationship: prompts execute the workflow, tools are the units of work, resources provide context. Prompts must integrate all three.
- TEMPLATE FORMAT: Use markdown with well-defined section names, not YAML frontmatter. Machine-readable through consistent section structure. Keep it simple - don't overcomplicate with YAML.
- DYNAMIC PROMPT READING: Prompts (like explore_idea) should be stable/static but READ from templates at runtime. Template acts as requirements spec - tells the prompt what questions to ask. Blog post template vs research paper template = different questions. Prompts should ask 2-5 questions at a time, stepping through them conversationally, not all at once.
- SHAPE/APPROACH EXAMPLES FOR BLOG POST: (1) Quick & Direct - short entry, minimal planning, just write and publish. (2) Structured Single Post - complex idea, needs development, one well-structured post. (3) Multi-Post Series - idea too big for one post, generate multiple posts with publishing strategy. Shape determines: one document or multiple? Quick or structured? The shape is the strategy for how the document(s) will be created and delivered.

## Constraints

- Must support specifying reference format requirements (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE, etc.)
- Must support structural requirements like table of contents, index, appendices
- Must allow providing example documents as style/tone references
- Must support both one-time documents (blog posts) and living documents (charters, standards) with continuous evolution
- Must support user-defined document type templates that modify the workflow and questions asked
- Must have distinct outline/structure phase between idea and draft, with outline remaining editable after draft creation
- Must ask user upfront about draft generation strategy (preserve user voice vs AI-generated vs hybrid)
- Revision tracking must use separate files (draft-v0.1.md, draft-v0.2.md, etc.) for initial implementation
- Must capture narrative conversation feedback similar to RiotPlan's feedback system - preserving deliberation about document decisions

## Questions

- What is the standard document lifecycle? Are there industry standards (ISO, IEEE, etc.) that define document states and transitions? **ANSWERED**: OASIS, IETF, W3C standards documented above.
- How should versioning work? Automatic version bumps on revision vs manual version control? What constitutes a "final" version vs ongoing revisions? **ANSWERED**: User-controlled, v0.x for drafts, v1.0 for published.
- Should the idea phase include narrative arc, argument structure, and section planning? Or does that belong in a separate "outline" phase? **ANSWERED**: Separate outline phase between idea and draft.
- How do we handle different document types (blog post, charter, reference doc, living standard) with potentially different lifecycles in the same system? **ANSWERED**: Document type templates that modify workflow.
- What built-in document types should ship with RiotDoc v1? **ANSWERED**: Blog post, podcast script (exist), email, project plan, research paper (need to add).
- How do users define custom document type templates? YAML config? JSON schema? What properties can be customized (fields, workflow stages, questions)? **PARTIAL**: Could be YAML, JSON, or Markdown - need to prototype.
- Should outline manipulation be command-based ("move section 3 before section 2") or interactive/visual? How does this work in MCP context? **ANSWERED**: Direct editing primary, optional MCP tools for programmatic changes.
- When does a draft version number increment? On every revision? On user command? What triggers v0.1 → v0.2 vs v1.0 → v1.1? **ANSWERED**: User-controlled increment.
- How do we handle the transition from "draft" (v0.x) to "published" (v1.0)? Is there an approval/finalization step? Who approves? **ANSWERED**: Single user decides, no complex workflow.
- For living documents that never reach "final", how do we distinguish between minor updates (typos) and major revisions (content changes)? **DEFERRED**: Not relevant for v1.
- Where is RiotPlan located? Need to reference its history and checkpoint implementation to copy into RiotDoc. **ANSWERED**: /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotplan

## Evidence

- RiotPlan source code at /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotplan
- RiotDoc source code at /Users/tobrien/gitw/kjerneverk/riotdoc
- Industry standards research (ISO/IEC/IEEE 26531:2023, RFC 3253, ISO 19475:2021)
- OASIS, IETF, W3C document lifecycle best practices
- [Email document template prototype - defines structure and questions for email documents](evidence/email-template.md)
- [Project plan document template prototype - defines structure and questions for project planning documents](evidence/project-plan-template.md)
- [Research paper document template prototype - defines structure and questions for academic/research papers](evidence/research-paper-template.md)
- [Blog post document template prototype (for comparison with existing implementation) - defines structure and questions](evidence/blog-post-template.md)
- [Podcast script document template prototype - defines structure and questions for podcast episodes with segments, timing, and production notes](evidence/podcast-script-template.md)

## Related Ideas

- RiotPlan feedback system (reference implementation)
- Document lifecycle management standards

# Shaping: [Name]

## Problem Statement

_What problem are we solving? What are we trying to achieve?_

## Approaches Considered

_Add approaches using riotplan_shaping_add_approach_

### Approach: Template-First with Copy-Paste Infrastructure

**Description**: Start by implementing the template system with lifecycle-aware questions as the foundation. Copy history/checkpoint/narrative code from RiotPlan into RiotDoc (accept duplication for now). Build all features together rather than incrementally. No shared library yet - that can come later when patterns stabilize.

**Tradeoffs**:
- Pro: Fast implementation - no need to create new packages or abstractions
- Pro: Templates drive the design - everything else fits around them
- Pro: Copy-paste is proven code that works in RiotPlan
- Pro: Can build and test everything together
- Con: Code duplication between RiotPlan and RiotDoc
- Con: If bugs found in shared code, need to fix in both places
- Con: Future refactoring needed when creating shared library
- Pro: Defers complexity - shared library when patterns are stable

**Assumptions**:
- Template system is the most important feature to get right
- Code duplication is acceptable short-term tradeoff for speed
- RiotPlan's history/checkpoint/narrative code works well enough to copy
- Shared library will be created eventually but not now


## Feedback

_Feedback will be added here as you provide it_

**Reasoning**: Speed is important. Templates drive the user experience and should be built first. Copy-paste history/checkpoint/narrative code from RiotPlan (accept duplication for now). Build all features together. No shared library yet - defer until patterns stabilize. This approach balances speed with quality and lets us iterate quickly.
